reviews.text: [i] “What we need is a few good taters. Boil 'em. Mash 'em. Stick 'em in a stew!”, wait, wrong game. This is Brotato from Temu, where instead of a potato, you play as a robot. It’s worse from both polish and replayability perspectives, but that doesn’t mean it’s not fun. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions, followed by the Review:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + 4 difficulties + 32 unique enemy types + 10 bots, each with distinct upgrade grid layouts + 19 weapons, 13 evolutions, and 84 upgrade modules, featuring a variety of damage types and stats to build around +Some stages come with dangers (acid rain, a sniper, rotating lasers, or drones), along with different goals (kill or survive) + Humour and personality e.g. a rubber ducky floating in a pool of lava, or toilet seat head armour 🟥 Cons: - Difficulty seems far too easy, as I’ve won 4 runs and lost 1 - There is no meta progression, so the longevity I love from the genre isn’t present - Enemies feel mostly the same on the first 2 difficulties before a sudden ramp up on difficulties 3 and 4 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ New audio tracks and maps ~ Meta progression would be a nice addition ~ Custom difficulty modifiers for extra bolts could be a fun addition ~ Changes to dashing, allowing for shorter dashes which use less than a full bar of energy ~ Not sure how I feel about large number of health drops, presently, the game feels too easy [h1] Brotato from Temu [/h1] Gunbot Diplomacy (GD) is Brotato, but instead of a potato, you're a robot (if the name didn't give it away). Each run begins with you picking a bot, starting weapon, and augment. Defeating enemies earns bolts which are spent on upgrades for your bots grid – Weapons, ammo, and augments. Levelling unlocks further perks that'll change how you play, such as additional damage for each second you stand still or transforming enemies into turrets on death. All the upgrades span across different tiers, represented by a simple colour system – teal, green, blue, purple, red. There's not much more to say – If you enjoyed Brotato, you'll have fun. 这种玩法太经典了，基本上怎么都不会腻，土豆兄弟都解锁的差不多了，来玩玩这个也是不错的

机械版土豆兄弟。整体机制类似，构筑主要靠多种武器和道具搭配。 特点： 1.有充能式闪避，可通过构筑减少冷却，增加充能点数。 2.装备道具栏有格子限制，并且相邻格子之间有影响。而且安装上去的装备不能再移动了，如果不合适只能卖掉。这一点给构筑带来更多的思考挺好的。 3.老版卡通片画风。 难度相比土豆兄弟要更大： 1.有地形限制。 2.除了血量和回血以外没有防御属性。 3.敌人种类多强度大，并且有大范围技能。 4.拾取零件(钱)范围非常小，要踩上去才行。 5.每一回合结束不会回满血，而且自身回复属性相比土豆要低不少。你好歹在BOSS回合回满血吧，或者每回合结束把油罐自动收集起来。 缺点或不合理处： 1.每回合结束的升级加点，不同等级的属性居然可以一起来。 2.有些升级属性明显不配他的等级，比如吃血包后加移速居然能给蓝色。（但是基于1影响又小多了） 3.每回合的钱很少。武器贵得要死，每回合的钱买一个武器都不一定够。 4.没有鼠标移动模式，wasd操作起来不是特别灵活。尤其是闪避方向太受限。 5.有些地形伤害和BOSS技能设计非常不合理。酸雨+恐龙+绿色爆炸球，设计师你自己玩过吗？还有那个超声波史莱姆，范围大还带减速，离谱。 6.战斗过程中不能暂停看自己的装备栏，升级的时候选择buff想看下武器吃哪些加成看不了。 7.道具装备图标的颜色辨识度太低，有的东西需要鼠标指上去看文字才知道是什么。 8.教程的文字说明是机翻，感觉在看天书。 9. 5级装备不能升级，但是还能把商店的东西装上去，白花钱。 10.操作手感不行：闪避作为重要躲避手段很多并不厚的墙还会把人卡主，或者沿着墙走的时候也会卡主，就不能让角色贴边走过去吗。 BUG： 鼠标放在图标上看解释文本，这时候战斗结束或结束暂停解释文本会一直卡在鼠标上。 开发组是想设计一个装备栏区域性构筑，但是由于游戏中金钱资源实在太少，再加上武器刷新没有和已有武器靠近的几率加成。导致前期只能是见武器就拿，没得挑。不然就会出现“刷不动怪→钱更少→武器差→刷不动怪”的恶性循环。 这游戏设计师就是来恶心人的，我真的服了。 在机制上恶心人就是肉鸽游戏最蠢的做法。一个肉鸽幸存者类游戏，玩家的重点应该主要是在构筑上，怎么样精打细算有限的金钱以及合理规划装备栏的位置。 而炮舰外交设计师很明显就是想通过诸如地形、酸雨、追踪攻击等手段考验玩家的操作。可是你角色的性能是个只会2次充能闪避的小可怜，不是Hades里的扎格列欧斯，没那么高的操作空间，也没有那么多的回复、防御手段。那些东西只会让玩家感到恶心，而不是高难度。尤其是在难度一里就已经同时拥有上面提到的那些限制。类吸血鬼幸存者游戏你好歹能让玩家专心构筑后期好好爽爽吧。 [hr][/hr] 设计师“我靠，你看我设计的这个史莱姆BOSS，高伤害，追踪弹，减速，多段伤害。玩家一定得操作得很牛逼才能打过” 实际上你的感受“满屏幕看不清的追踪弹，还要附带减速。BOSS那减速+大范围+多段伤害光圈，外加减速追踪弹，没闪避能给你一套打10+血。我草了” 游戏最大的几个问题：金钱、回复手段、怪物机制，更新计划提都没提。 好好的游戏底子整的稀烂，抄都不会抄。

[h1] 土豆兄弟+邻近强化[/h1] 《炮舰外交》是一款“幸存者like”游戏，即在潮水般的敌人中生存、升级、构建强力输出体系。 本作的游戏模式类似“土豆兄弟”的短局多轮，商店消费+经验升级，但并没有那么细分的道具与经济类属性；build形式上则融入了些许《背包乱斗》背包空间与邻近强化的风味，通过商店购买模块，将武器与被动构建在六边形网络背包下，每个模块的效能受周边模块影响增益。 [h1] 游戏内容简介[/h1] 流程方面，每局游戏19轮、3个固定boss、4种难度分层，敌人有蛮多的远程冲锋自爆类型，有一定难度，不太好站撸。 内容方面，目前游戏具有10名角色、19种武器模块、32种被动模块、83种角色升级被动。包括有13种特定模块的组合能诞生高级的进化武器、也有待玩家自行摸索。譬如“加特林”和“冷却缩减”就能进化出无视位置、获得所有被动模块增益的彩虹加特林。 Roguelite属性方面，无局外货币的局外属性养成，但仍需通过完成特定目标/成就的方式、逐步解锁道具。 背包空间也有一定的随机性，背包形状随机、以及部分格子会提供额外增益。 美术中规中矩，但优化感觉一般。 [h1] 体验：既有框架内微创新[/h1] 相比于绝大多其他类型的游戏，幸存者like的一大优势就在于制作简单、创意也不用想太多、在子系统上做些差异即可；由于制作成本相对较低，即便销量表现并不乐观，开发团队也无需承担过多风险，更不用说万一就火了呢？以至于即便在该类浪潮已经退去的如今，仍能不时看到好几款新上市的幸存者like。 本作也是如此，整体并未在现有的幸存者like框架下做出改革式的变动，保留了核心的割草升级生存体验，创新更多体现在对局部系统的调整，通过build形式的变通在同质化赛道上寻求一丝差异化的吸引力。但个人感觉，本作build模式的虽然通过“邻近强化”提升了些许策略性，整体差异性却还是不够显著，尤其是在背包系统是固定镶嵌的形式、无法自由整理，就极大降低了背包管理的趣味性。 [h1]总结[/h1] 《炮舰外交》仍是一款以微创新塑造差异化的幸存者like作品，整体虽然仍是幸存者like常规体验占据主导地位、不能带来焕然一新的改革性超越，但通过对现有build形式的创新，用邻近强化的六边形模块系统让构筑多了几分空间规划的策略感，对于依旧喜爱这类割草生存模式的玩家而言，仍不妨入手尝试一番这些新花样。 [quote]加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]咱的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来游戏体验分享，也期待您来一起分享自己的游戏体验干货~[/quote]

《炮舰外交》是这么一款和《土豆兄弟》很类似的幸存者类动作肉鸽闯关游戏，游戏里我们将化身各种废土世界的战争机器，面对四周蜂拥而来的各种怪物，使用手中各种武器最大程度的消灭来犯之敌，存活下来。再利用各种升级获取的各种模块和商店购买的武器配件组合，构筑更为强大的战斗BD，消灭更多的怪物，让自己成为废土世界让怪物闻风丧胆的死亡泰坦！ 《炮舰外交》有着10种样式各异、战斗特长各不相同的机器人给我们解锁使用，再从十八种武器（同样需要战斗解锁）里选择一个顺手的当初始武器，不一样的武器有着不一样的攻击机制，远程、近身、群攻、专一等等应有尽有，让我们每次战斗都能有完全不一样的战斗体验，主打一个爽到停不下来！ 游戏的每个小关卡战斗结束我们都能获得一次“模块”多抽1的机会，这些“模块”其实就是其他爬塔游戏里的“遗物”的意思，有着不同的等阶，可以给我们的小机器人提供许多强大的被动。不过游戏主要的玩法还是在于每次选完配件之后的“商店”环节，在这里我们购买了的武器和部件是需要安装进左边的棋盘里才能生效，然后各种武器和部件相互之间都会有各种羁绊一类的作用，同样的武器和部件放一起还能升级，特定的武器和部件在一起还能进化，再将这棋盘内的成长与模块联系来构成完整的战斗BD，这玩法多到有点废脑袋！ 整体而言，《炮舰外交》就是这么一款不服就干的幸存者类动作肉鸽闯关游戏，让我们发动脑力构筑战斗BD，在一刻都不停歇的战斗中战胜敌人并存活到最后，成为让所有怪物都战栗的废土世界死亡泰坦吧！ [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

I really wanted to like this game but it just didn’t click for me. A lot of the fun in these games is executing different builds and seeing what works, but despite my best efforts I was never able to get into a good groove with that in this one because it seemed like no matter what I did the results were the same. I think there is potential for this game to be good and maybe I was just playing it wrong, but for now I don’t feel much compulsion to keep playing it.

I'm sure this could be fun in the future, but as-is it is just ... meh. It is a Brotato-like in that you buy items and get level ups to add stats to face increasingly difficult hordes of enemies. Unlike Brotato there are different "types" of missions with the primary two being survival (don't die) and destroy (kill X enemies), but honestly it's a distinction without a difference at this point. While it plays like Brotato, it has a few "unique" additions which are an equipment grid which allows you to place weapons and upgrades in a hex-based grid that changes from game to game, and in having evolutions for weapons which greatly impact how the grid placement works. There is a dodge. The UI is also surprisingly polished where you can see which stats will impact what which is unexpected yet appreciated. That said, the game just doesn't have much going for it. It lacks depth. The feeling of the game is more frustration than fun for character movement and hit detection. So many of the weapons are a struggle and the shop/level-up RNG just feels too outsized to have the challenge turn to fun or feel surmountable even on the easiest difficulties. Maybe in a half year if they add updates and balance it could be good, but as is? No thanks.

游戏还有很大的进步空间，首先每波所能获得的资源实在太少了，商店里的东西买不起，1级的武器价格过高，导致角色成长跟不上敌人成长。修理属性给的回复太少了根本不能适配战斗，而且每波结束后不能完全回血，资源吸取范围又小，就不能波次快结束时靠血量换资源，成长跟不上，买不起东西，打不死敌人，小心走位不敢吸资源，完全恶性循环。战斗中也不能看角色装备配置。游戏的思路很好但战斗舒适度比土豆兄弟差太多了。整体评价是想要哪怕跟上土豆兄弟的段位也有很长的路要走，如果作者能优化的话还是未来可期的。

very fun game but I cant give it a good review until they add detail explanations of how the game mechanics work for example you can evolve weapons in the game but how do you do that? Nobody knows I tried to google it and got nothing useful the only information the game gives you is that it involves upgrades that are level three or higher or augments and it only told me that after i accidentally did it once for the first time untill that point its gives you zero information and regardless i have yet to manage to repeat it since I have no f'n clue how to trigger an evolution. long story short if you don't like games that have complicated upgrade system that refuse to explain how those systems work don't buy this game. I hope they add some better tutorials and explanations because I genuinely like the game but it extremely frustrating when I waste hard earned upgrade materials that only drop based on rng just trying to figure out what order i need to combine things to trigger an evolution and it never works

Truth to be told, I've never been a fan of roguelikes and roguelites. My expierence boils down to playing Loop Hero, which has it's own unique elements, including a story. Nevertheless, I've played Gunbot Diplomacy demo some time ago. I dunno if love for robots (steambots?) made me do it or I finally decided to give the genre a proper try. I've played it and I liked it. Here I am, playing the full version. As it often the case with the genre, there's no story. The "story" boils down to: you’re a robot in a wasteland, and everything (slimes, mutants, drones, angry office workers?) wants you dead. Why? No one knows and no one cares. It's roguelite, you're here to blow stuff up and get stronger with each levels. Visuals aren't bad. Enemy designs are: imagine radioactive slimes, cactus-crab hybrids, and laser-firing bots, all colorful and detailed, although it's not like you have time to give them a proper look. As you upgrade your Gunbot, it visibly evolves from a scrappy heap to a weapon-covered monstrosity, which is cool as well. Maps, however, are hit-or-miss. While hazards like acid rain glow vividly, environments are simplistic, lack detail and often repear. Since we're here for gameplay, what's on offer? The Upgrade Grid is a cool feature: weapons, augments, and boosters slot into a hex grid. Placement matters: put a machine gun next to a "Thumper" augment, and its cooldown drops 20%. Unlock evolved weapons like nuke-launching footballs by combining specific items. Although it's not often clear what do you need to combine to receive a "super" version of any selected weapon. Progression & Unlocks: Start with one bot (the "All-Rounder") and nine weapons. Win runs to unlock 10+ bots and 80+ modules. Each bot slightly changes your playstyle, some bots have affinity for different damage type, some have more health, but your fighting loop is always the same: run, dodge, gather oil canisters, while kill the enemies. Combat & Controls: Weapons auto-target, so you focus on dodging via dash moves. It’s frantic but fair post-patch: infamous enemies like charging "Dillosaurs" now give you time to react. Scavenge oil cans for health and scrap for upgrades between waves. It's not all sunshine and rainbows tho. Runs can feel repetitive early on, with small maps and similar objectives (survive X time/kill X enemies). The soundtrack pumps upbeat electronic tunes that match the chaos but won’t stick in your head. Weapon sound effects are fine. As always with these games, Gunbot Diplomacy nails the "just one more run" hook. Grid system and random drops between missions are often enough to keep you playing. Considering the price, this is a good game that'll fill a couple of your lonely evenings. Warning: Review is overly complicated and long. If you don't like that, don't read this. This review was made as of Infinite Loop, and I will maybe update it. May and WILL contain outdated information. Now that I've wasted 20 seconds of your life, let's start. Part 1: General Overview Gunbot Diplomacy is a game that faces you, a Gunbot, against hordes of slimes, robots, mutants, and The Big Fricken' Gunbot. Part 2: Mechanics Health: Self-explanatory. Repair: Whatever this number's value is, is how much health you restore at the end of a Map, 25 seconds in the Map, or Leveling up. If you have 4 Repair, you get +4 health at the end of a Map, and so on. Critical Chance: Self-explanatory. Crits by default do +200% damage. There are also different forms of weapons: Impact, simple. They deal damage when the weapon's projectile (or fist... if you use the Thumper Weapon System.) hits an enemy. Periodic: These deal damage over time. Explosive: ...Do I need to explain? Construct: I do not know. Upgrade Grids: Instead of having limitations, like only 6 weapons/upgrades each, you can put these on your Upgrade Grid. Use Scrap (dropped from killed enemies, how do slimes drop metal when they have bone inside them??) to buy upgrades and Weapon Systems. When you place a thing on the grid, it'll stay there until you sell it. You can place a duplicate (like another Shotgun on top of a Shotgun) to upgrade it, to a maximum of 5 times. Higher quality things get more expensive, and prices increase further into your run. Modules: When you Level up, or pick up a Toolbox, you can choose a Module. (Due to my lazy self, I'm not going over the Modules and Upgrades, minus a few important ones.) Toolboxes: They give +1 Module selection, plus higher chances for rarer Modules. The orange number below your scrap indicates scrap you did not pick up. When you pick up that amount, it's doubled. (You get all the scrap.) A few modules/upgrades to pick: Machine Learning: +20% more XP for killing, Level Up faster. Trusty Tailgunner: Essentially an extra weapon. Repurpose: Killing enemies has a chance (increase with Luck) to turn an enemy to a turret for a certain amount of time. (Increase this time with Duration.) Auto-Cannon: A static assistance. Easter egg: Even when you die, it is still possible to get kills. Therefore, if you're patient enough, you can kill the BFG with your turrets. Threebuild: Technically Fourbuild, it gives 4 bonuses. Upgrades: Explosive ammo: Every hit has a chance to explode, dealing extra damage. Area of explosion can be increased with Area upgrades/Modules. Cryo-Core Ammo: Slows hit targets down, stacks 3 times. Incendiary Ammo: Hits have a chance to light the target on fire, dealing Periodic damage. Cyclone Ammo: Hits have a chance to create a tornado, dealing damage to those within its area. Part 3: Bots Fair warning: I only have knowledge on All-Rounder and Lucky. (Lance-Bot if we include Blast Off, but that was a preview. Sleepy Sentry probably modified it.) All-Rounder: Go-to for runs. Lucky: Start with Luck-based Augment (well...) of your choosing attached to your starter weapon. Every time you pick up an Oil Canister, you get +2 Luck, which resets at the end of a Map. You can still get Luck Modules, which will not reset. (So if you got to 19 Luck off of 15 Luck, at the end of the Map, you're back to 15 Luck.) Part 4: Weapons Here are just a few weapons to get yourself acquainted with before you start brutally murdering the local Sublime Slime population. Machine Gun: Fires bullets that deal Impact damage. Gatling Gun: Machine Gun, but faster. Shotgun: Fires a spread of bullets, dealing Impact Damage. Landmines: A explosive that activates when an enemy touches them. Rocket Launcher: Shoots a rocket that deals Explosive damage. Missile Swarm: A bunch of mini-rockets that home in on random enemies. Dodge Puddle: When Dodging (Spacebar on M&K), you leave behind a field that deals damage. Decoy Launcher: A decoy (which attracts enemies to it) is launched, attracting enemies, and when it runs out of health, KA-BOOM! Part 5: Enemies As I've mentioned enemies a lot, why aren't I talking about them? Well, here they are. Sublime Slimes: Not really threatening. 1 Damage per hit. Smort Slimes: Their smort. Please don't insult them. Dillosaur: F*** these things. Boss Slime: When you learn the attacks, he's quite easy. Boss Slime Sr: Uh... NUH UH. B. F. G.: The Big Fricken' Gunbot. Part 6: Ratings Gameplay?: 10/10 Soundtrack?: 100000/10. Difficulty?: 9/10. Fairness?: Dillosaur/10 (how much you can reel back from mistakes) Overall?: 10/10. Part 7: Summary Gunbot Diplomacy has unique mechanics, tools-of-mass-destruction, and Smort slimes. Part 8: Closing Words. Wow, can't believe I typed all that within an hour. Sir Shootsalot once said: "I shoot a lot." Which matches Gunbot Diplomacy a lot. You shoot a lot.

---See where this game landed on my Survivor Rogue-lite Tier List beneath this review!--- Decent Survivor Roguelike somewhat in the vein of [b]Brotato[/b] (I prefer the runs in this game though). It also reminds me of [b]Slime 3k: Rise Against Despot[/b]. There's a free version of Gunbot Diplomacy that you can try first to see if it's for you. I really enjoy the progression through a run. A run comprises of about 20 short stages. Between stages you choose level up bonuses and build your bot by buying weapons and augments and slotting them in. Where you place things into your bot matters, as you try to synergize things together. Weapons and augments can be upgraded by placing the same weapon/augments on top of each other. If you have the correct weapon + augment combination, your weapon can evolve into a special, superior version (just like in Vampire Survivors). [b]Gunbot Diplomacy[/b] is a fun time, with just enough going on to make it more interesting to me than 95% of the games I've tried in the survivors genre. IF NOT "BROTATO", WHY "BROTATO" SHAPED?! Do you LOVE Brotato? I mean it. Do you LOVE Brotato? If not, A: Close this page and play Brotato somewhere, then come back. B: Play Brotato until you are tired of Brotato, then come back to this review. If you answered YES to "Do you LOVE Brotato?" have I got a game for you. Gunbot Diplomacy is a different Brotato, slightly worse in just about every respect, but a solid game that I ended up enjoying and playing way more than I expected I would. But if you've played the HECK out of Brotato and just want something slightly different/the thrill of unlocking different stuff and finding other combos, you could do a lot worse than Gunbot Diplomacy. If you've made it this far, you know the drill - GD is a top-down shoot 'em up roguelite where you kill things, collect currency, and get random upgrades. It's got far less characters, enemies and bosses, though a surprisingly large amount of upgrades. The main difference is a hex shaped upgrade combo system, which is good news and bad news. It gives you some more options and variety, but makes shifting to a new build or strategy late game nearly impossible because you're already locked in to so many tied together upgrades. There's also a lot of confusion as to what works with what, what DOES what, and what effects are actually happening - as the game can be a bit visually a clusterf, and the tooltips aren't always super clear. There's MAJOR balance issues (a couple of the upgrades are way way way way more powerful than others), but if you can avoid just picking the OP stuff, you can have some fun with combos and other varieties of items, just seeing what works and what works together. I'm not going to complicate things. If you love Brotato, and want a little more Brotato but slightly different, Gunbot Diplomacy is for you. If not, you're better served by Brotato.

[b]GUNBOT DIPLOMACY[/b], is a inventory management round based survivors-like that is playing a tough balancing game between simplicity and a lot of complexity. This game is clearly inspired by Brotato and most of the mechanics within the game are very similar. Most of the game, is about managing a hex grid that acts as your inventory, storing all your weapons and modifications to those weapons. Gunbot Diplomacy does make an attempt to make the management a litte easier but highlighting relevant components but the distinction between highlighted and non-highlighted items are far too little and make it quite hard to use. The classes, weapons, and perks are quite limted and may make the game quite boring quicky. It is not a bad game at all, the grid system is unique and not overwhelming. The upgrades are mostly easy to understand and the combat just follows the traditional auto aim and pick up drops gameplay. The combat is satisfying and the gameplay is extremely smooth with zero bugs. If you want more round-based twin sticks, then this is definitely a game to pick up. [b]PROS[/b]: - Fun upgrade system - Not unfairly challenging - Good price point - Great little achievements [b]CONS[/b]: - Difficult to see highlights - Little replaybility especially for a roguelike [i]It is pretty astonishing that you get tired of this type of roguelike game in around 10 hours.[/i]

Very grindy roguelike. What it does different than most other similar survivor clones, is a grid-like structure for placing weapons and upgrades. Environments and enemy variety are lacking and the art style isn't very appealing or clear. The main issue is... I just don't have any control over my build or my damage output. The concept is great, the grid system is really cool on paper, but when all you get are random items, it really doesn't matter how you place them next to each other. There is just no planning possible and quite often I got stuck with a bad combination, because everything is luck based. ...and the metaprogression is directly tied to this system, so it feels like the game is artificially extending its gameplay, without providing any mechanical depth to compensate.
